title: Block 1 Knowledge Check — Professional Judgement, Live Conduct and Calibration

questions.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of recurrent examiner professional development?

answers.text: Repeat the initial Examiner Course every two years.
Maintain currency, reflection, evidence discipline and examiner calibration.
Ensure every examiner uses an identical assessment technique.
Replace the examiner’s responsibility to remain current with regulatory material.

questions.feedback: Correct response: B. Recurrent development assumes foundational knowledge is already established. Its purpose is to maintain current, reflective and standardised professional practice.

questions.question: An experienced examiner’s professional intuition:

answers.text: Can replace recorded evidence when the examiner is highly experienced.
Should never influence an assessment.
Can help recognise patterns, but conclusions must still be supported by evidence and standards.
Is more reliable than the published assessment standard.

questions.feedback: Correct response: C. Experience can sharpen recognition, but assessment conclusions must remain anchored to observable evidence and the applicable standard.

questions.question: You are assessing a familiar, well-regarded candidate while the operator is short of qualified personnel. Which information should carry the greatest weight?

answers.text: The candidate’s previous strong performance.
The operator’s confidence in the candidate.
The observable evidence from today’s assessment.
The operational consequences of an unsuccessful outcome.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: C. Previous performance and operational context may influence the examiner, but they do not replace evidence from the current assessment.

questions.question: A candidate enters one digit of a radio frequency incorrectly, then independently identifies and corrects it after no response. What is the best examiner response?

answers.text: Treat the error itself as evidence that the required standard has not been met.
Continue the assessment and consider the error, recognition and recovery in context with the rest of the evidence.
Ignore the event completely because communication was eventually established.
Immediately tell the candidate which digit was entered incorrectly.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: B. The error is observable evidence, but its significance depends on context, recognition, independence, recovery, recurrence and the applicable standard. Recovery adds evidence; it does not erase the original error.

questions.question: A highly experienced candidate has strong technical skill, the operator is short of personnel, and a significant lapse in judgement appears near the end of the assessment. Which question should the examiner answer first?

answers.text: Will the operator be able to replace the candidate?
Is the candidate usually competent?
What exactly was observed, and which standard or competency does it relate to?
Would failing the candidate be disproportionate after an otherwise strong test?

questions.feedback: Preferred response: C. The decision process must begin with observable evidence and its relationship to the standard, not operational consequence or reputation.

questions.question: The evidence is significant but isolated, and there is no further valid opportunity to gather more evidence. Which statement is most appropriate?

answers.text: An isolated event can never determine an assessment outcome.
A single event may be decisive if its severity and relationship to the standard justify that weight.
Strong technical performance should always outweigh one judgement concern.
The candidate should automatically receive the benefit of the doubt.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: B. Pattern matters, but severity matters too. Consider context, consequence, independence, recovery and the precise requirements of the standard.

questions.question: Which debrief statement is more defensible?

answers.text: I don’t think you showed enough situational awareness today.
During the arrival you did not identify the conflicting traffic despite two opportunities, and the scan was not re-established until after the traffic alert.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: B. It describes observable behaviour and provides a clearer evidence trail for the assessment judgement.

questions.question: In the mixed-evidence workshop, an administrative prerequisite appears incomplete although the operator says the underlying training was completed. What should drive the commencement decision?

answers.text: Likely candidate competence.
Operational need.
Whether the required preconditions for a valid assessment are actually satisfied.
The examiner’s previous knowledge of the candidate.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: C. Competence and assessment validity are related but separate. Confirm that the assessment can legitimately commence within current requirements and authority.

questions.question: During a later high-workload phase, the candidate misses a radio call, omits one checklist item and allows navigation accuracy to deteriorate. Each event is recoverable. What should the examiner do?

answers.text: Fail immediately because three errors have occurred.
Ignore the issues because each was recoverable.
Continue gathering evidence and assess whether the events form a meaningful workload or situational-awareness pattern.
Prompt the candidate to manage workload better.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: C. Separate isolated error from emerging pattern. Prompting may contaminate evidence unless needed for safety.

questions.question: During a later phase, the candidate enters a frequency incorrectly, initially repeats the call, then independently identifies and corrects the entry. Which statement is most accurate?

answers.text: The incorrect frequency automatically determines the final result.
The event should be ignored because the candidate eventually corrected it.
Assess the error, recognition and recovery as part of the complete evidence story and determine whether it is isolated or contributes to a wider pattern.
Immediately provide the correct frequency whenever a radio entry error occurs.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: C. The incorrect entry, recognition and independent recovery are all relevant evidence. Avoid an automatic outcome based on one procedural error.

questions.question: After a frequency error, the candidate demonstrates stronger cross-checking and performs the remaining items well. How should the recovery be treated?

answers.text: It erases the earlier error.
It is irrelevant because an error occurred.
It provides useful evidence, but must be weighed alongside the original event rather than replacing it.
It guarantees competence because the candidate corrected the problem.

questions.feedback: Preferred response: C. Recovery can demonstrate recognition, checking discipline and effective correction, but it does not remove the original evidence.

questions.question: When operational pressure exists, which factor should determine the assessment standard applied?

answers.text: Candidate experience.
Operator need.
Published requirements and current assessment evidence.
Examiner familiarity.

questions.feedback: Correct response: C. Operational pressure may be real, but it does not alter the applicable standard or the evidence required.

questions.question: What is the best description of examiner drift in this programme?

answers.text: Any development in examiner technique.
Gradual movement away from shared interpretation or application of the required standard.
A formal CAA enforcement action.
Any disagreement between two examiners.

questions.feedback: Correct response: B. Professional practice should evolve. Drift refers to movement away from shared standards or their consistent application.

questions.question: A candidate enters an incorrect frequency, recognises it independently and corrects it. What should the examiner do?

answers.text: Ignore the original error because recovery occurred.
Treat the error as an automatic failure.
Consider both the error and the recovery in context with the wider evidence and applicable standard.
Repeat the exercise until it is performed correctly.

questions.feedback: Correct response: C. The original error and the independent recovery are both relevant evidence and must be considered with the wider assessment pattern and standard.

questions.question: How should strong recovery after an error be treated?

answers.text: It always cancels the original error.
It is irrelevant.
It is additional evidence that must be weighed with the original event.
It automatically changes a fail to a pass.

questions.feedback: Correct response: C. Recovery may demonstrate recognition and resilience, but it does not erase the original evidence.

questions.question: Which note is most defensible?

answers.text: Poor judgement.
Weak situational awareness.
Continued approach after agreed stabilisation criteria were not met.
Candidate seemed stressed.

questions.feedback: Correct response: C. The strongest note records specific observable behaviour that can be linked to the standard.
